node.title: Re: Integer regex, different results in windows and mac - I just need regex help
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Just to confirm what the others have said, if you save your file with CRLF line endings on a system that uses LF line endings (*NIX, including Mac OS X) and run it, it gives the wrong results. If you then put binmode DATA, ':crlf'; just before the loop, it works again. :crlf is the default on Windows, see [doc://open] and [doc://binmode], and it causes the CRLF line endings to be converted to LF, so that [doc://chomp] works properly. Without :crlf, what is happening is that $num contains a trailing CRLF, but [doc://chomp] only removes the LF, leaving the strings looking like "19\r", which you can see yourself if you use [mod://Data::Dump] or [doc://Data::Dumper] with $Data::Dumper::Useqq=1; - see also the [id://745674]. The best solution IMO is to convert the file to LF line endings, for example using fromdos from the [http://www.thefreecountry.com/tofrodos/index.shtml|Tofrodos] package, and also many text editors support selecting the line endings in the "Save As" dialog.

Also, regarding your regexes, I just wanted to point out [mod://Regexp::Common::number], which you might find useful, and also that the regex /^[0].{0}/ looks a little suspicious: .{0} doesn't really do anything, and rewriting the regex as /^0/ shows that it will accept any string beginning with a 0, including stuff like "0 but true", is that really what you want?
